text:
Maria: Quick follow-up to the console access-filtering RFC. Proposal: move tenant access gating out of gateway pre-filter and into projection output so we can enable cursor-anchored shared caching for hotspot dashboard panels. Short thread on tradeoffs + cutover plan.

AJ: Curious — moving auth later sounds risky. Wouldn't we be doing more work before we know a request is allowed?

Maria: Yes, we may do extra compute, but benefit is cache reuse across tenants when panel outputs are tenant-agnostic. Currently pre-filter bakes tenant context into upstream work so caches are single-tenant only.

Tessa: Can you sketch the RPC path change? I want to see where tenant id flows.

Maria: Current: client -> gateway (auth+perm pre-filter) -> query-service -> projection -> panel.
Proposed: client -> gateway (auth token pass-through) -> query-service -> projection (auth-check + output-filter) -> panel/cache.

Drew: Major concern is that projections now might materialize larger intermediate sets before applying tenant mask. Memory and CPU could spike for some panels.

Maria: Mitigations we discussed: per-projection memory+cpu quotas; projection sandboxing; limit materialization via streaming masks where possible; opt-in shared caching only when projection declares tenant-agnostic outputs.

Sam: How do you decide cache key semantics? Need to avoid accidental cross-tenant reuse.

Maria: Cache key proposal: [panel_id, query_hash, cursor_bucket, projection_version, tenant_mask_token?]. tenant_mask_token empty => eligible for shared cache; non-empty => single-tenant.

AJ: Implementation API idea: projection exposes two publish modes: publish_shared(key, payload, proof) and publish_private(key, tenant_id, payload). Shared path requires a proof blob from a static analyzer that verifies output schema and that no tenant-scoped columns are present.

Tessa: We'll need console/ops controls to mark panels sensitive by default so shared publish is disabled unless explicitly approved. Also UI to surface which panels are using shared caching.

Drew: Perf expectations? ballpark wins for hotspot panels?

Maria: Synthetic playground numbers: enabling shared cache with 30s TTL + cursor-anchored keys gives ~2.0-2.8x throughput on heavy panels and p95 latency improvement ~30-40% under contended load. Materialization memory increase depends on panel complexity; we can cap with quotas.

Sam: Threat model? If projection process is compromised we must ensure no cross-tenant leakage even when shared caches exist.

AJ: I'll draft threat-model notes covering sandbox escape, cache poisoning, replay attacks, and proof forgery. Probably require HSM-backed signing for proof token before accepting shared publish.

Maria: Proposal for "proof" lifecycle: projection static analyzer outputs declaration (output-scols, projection_version, allowed_ops) -> signed by build/validator -> cache accepts shared publish only with valid signature. Validator fails if any tenant-scoped field detected.

Tessa: Ops can have a console flag: default-disable-shared-cache, per-panel override with audit log. Also add a rule to auto-disable shared for panels referencing dataset type "sensitive_*".

Drew: Cutover plan (ops-bot suggested): Canary 10% tenant traffic + 5 hotspot panels -> monitor cache-hit ratio, auth-failure alerts, memory footprint -> expand 50% -> global. Rollback if any auth anomaly or cache-poisoning signal.

ops-bot: deploy-plan captured: canary -> monitor metrics: cache_hit_rate, auth_checks_failed, projection_mem_violation, p95_latency -> promote if green.

Sam: Action items: Maria: PR for projection cache API + proof token spec. AJ: threat-model doc + HSM signing proposal. Tessa: console UI flags + sensitive-panel classification. Drew: perf harness to measure materialization footprints and streaming-mask feasibility.

Maria: I'll post the PR draft by EOD and tag folks. Thanks all :thumbsup:
